text:
maria: heads-up: p95/p99 spike hitting hosted-us-east-1 around 15:12 UTC. customer reports slow responses. saw a sharp queue depth climb on batcher for model-x-small :thinking_face:

runtime-bot: alert: p99_latency > 1200ms for route /v1/generate on hosted-us-east-1 (15:12:24). generated incident id inc-203577

kai: grabbing initial metrics. queue_depth by shard: 40 -> 420 within 2m, batch_size median bumped from 8 -> 42. weirdly, seq_len distribution shifted up (more long-context requests).

maria: any recent rollouts? no deploys in last hour. config changes?

drew: nothing in deploys. infra notes one noisy tenant on the same GPU pool earlier — tenant: search-ops. Could that be noisy neighbor causing kernel mismatch?

sam: posting profiler snapshot from the slow instance: 
```
kernel_selector: chosen_kernel=matmul_f16_fast heuristic=latency_opt
observed_seq_len_p50=256 p95=1024
fallback_count=18 -> fallback_kernel=int8_generic
kv_cache_evictions=1200/min
batcher_queue_depth=520
cpu_scheduling_wait_ms=48
```

kai: looks like kernel selector flipped heuristics mid-spike. selector logs show it tried latency_opt then had many fallbacks to int8_generic which is slower in our path for this model. fallback triggered due to quantization mismatch when seq_len>512.

maria: that explains increased latency. fallbacks + cache evictions = longer setup per request. do we have exact kernel logs?

sam: paste of /var/log/runtime/kernel-selector.log snippet: 
```
15:11:58 [INFO] seq_len_est=128 -> use matmul_f16_fast
15:12:10 [WARN] seq_len_est jump: 128 -> 900, switching heuristic
15:12:11 [INFO] attempting matmul_int8_opt
15:12:12 [ERROR] matmul_int8_opt: kernel_missing_for_variant -> fallback int8_generic
15:12:12 [INFO] fallback latency=320ms
```

drew: so two interacting issues: upstream request pattern shift (longer contexts) + kernel inventory doesn't have a low-latency int8 kernel for the new path -> fallback to generic slow kernel. Also batcher rewarded larger batches which increases tail latency when fallback occurs.

kai: quick mitigation: force kernel selector to stay on conservative kernel for model-x-small in hosted-us-east-1: set KERNEL_SELECTOR_FORCE=matmul_f16_fast for pool hosted-us-east-1:poolA. That avoids fallback churn. I'll push a patch to the runtime flags.

maria: also reduce batcher max window for that pool from 200ms -> 80ms to keep queue depth down while we stabilize. Can we do both now?

sam: doing the kernel flag change: `curl -X POST https://controlplane/flags -d '{"pool":"hosted-us-east-1:poolA","KERNEL_SELECTOR_FORCE":"matmul_f16_fast"}'` -> 204 OK. runtime reported flag applied at 15:22:05.

drew: reducing batcher window: `POST /platform/pools/poolA/config {"batcher.max_window_ms":80}` -> applied at 15:23:10.

runtime-bot: info: config change applied for poolA (flags, batcher) at 15:23:10. Monitoring p95/p99...

maria: monitoring dashboards — queue_depth dropping: 520 -> 60 over 4m. p95 dropped from 1100ms -> 240ms. p99 still slightly elevated at ~520ms but trending down. :thumbsup:

kai: follow-up: need a durable fix — either add an optimized int8 kernel path for these long contexts or tune kernel selector thresholds to consider fallback cost. Also add preflight canary detecting sudden seq_len distribution shifts to avoid churn.

sam: also saw KV cache churn metric spike; we'll add an eviction cap alarm when evictions/sec > 200 to trigger circuit-breaker to prefer latency-safe kernels.

maria: agreed. create a ticket for kernel onboarding + canary. assign to eng-runtime and eng-ml. I'll document the incident notes and timeline.

drew: created ticket PERF-1038: "model-x-small: int8 kernel onboarding and selector threshold hardening" — assigned kai/drew, due EOW.

maria: closing this thread for now, will keep monitoring. great quick ops. :tada:
